body:
Try upgrading to the latest SqlSrv drivers (3.2), AFAIK, PHP x64 does not play nice with Windows!

What happens if you run that query directly in the SQL management studio?

@dakota 
Before reporting, I've searched for a more recent one but could not find any (64-bit ones).
Can you try running the query directly in the management console? That would at least narrow down where the problem is coming from.

@dakota 
done

```
C:\>sqlcmd

1> use GateIP_01
2> GO
Changed database context to 'GateIP_01'.
1> SELECT * FROM (
2> SELECT [HardwareEvents].[ObjectId] AS [HardwareEvents__ObjectId],
3>  [HardwareEvents].[Msg] AS [HardwareEvents__Msg],
4>   [HardwareEvents].[DateTime] AS [HardwareEvents__DateTime],
5>    (ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY NULL)
6>    ) AS [_cake_page_rownum_]
7>     FROM [HardwareEvent] [HardwareEvents]) _cake_paging_
8>     WHERE _cake_paging_._cake_page_rownum_ <= 100
9> GO
Сообщение 5309, уровень 16, состояние 1, сервер SKD-SRV\SQLEXPRESS, строка 5
Windowed functions do not support constants as ORDER BY clause expressions.
1>
```
Fantastic, so we've excluded the driver from the equation :) Seems like Cake is generating an invalid query then. Will take a look and let you know.
@dmromanov can you change the query so it reads "ORDER BY SELECT NULL" ?

@lorenzo 

```
1> SELECT * FROM (SELECT [HardwareEvents].[ObjectId] AS [HardwareEvents__ObjectId], [HardwareEvents].[Msg] AS [HardwareEvents__Msg], [HardwareEvents].[DateTime] AS [HardwareEvents__DateTime], (ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY SELECT NULL)) AS [_cake_page_rownum_] FROM [HardwareEvent] [HardwareEvents]) _cake_paging_ WHERE _cake_paging_._cake_page_rownum_ <= 100
2> GO
Сообщение 156, уровень 15, состояние 1, сервер SKD-SRV\SQLEXPRESS, строка 1
Incorrect syntax near the keyword 'SELECT'.
```
odd, because that is the way cake 2 used to work
@dmromanov can you add parens like "ORDER BY (SELECT NULL)"

@lorenzo 
It worked

```
1> SELECT * FROM (SELECT [HardwareEvents].[ObjectId] AS [HardwareEvents__ObjectId], [HardwareEvents].[Msg] AS [HardwareEvents__Msg], [HardwareEvents].[DateTime] AS [HardwareEvents__DateTime], (ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY (SELECT NULL))) AS [_cake_page_rownum_] FROM [HardwareEvent] [HardwareEvents]) _cake_paging_ WHERE _cake_paging_._cake_page_rownum_ <= 100
2> GO

*Query result*
```

I remember testing this pagination query generation, but it might have been with 2010 & forcing the code down this path. Seems strange that the existing code would work in 2010 but not 2008. I can take another look as there are a few other windows/sqlserver issues now.

I've also experienced this problem in MSSQL 2008 but in MSSQL 2014 it works fine. So it must be the version. I'd like to keep the support also for 2008 since it is still a standart on many production servers.
